topics.label: Lecture introduction and learning outcomes
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer welcomes the class, connects the upcoming material to previous histopathology practicals, and outlines the learning outcomes for the session.

topics.label: Tumor virology, proto-oncogene discovery, and transformation assays
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics trace how the study of transforming viruses revealed cellular proto-oncogenes and led to experimental assays for testing the oncogenic capacity of altered genes.

topics.label: Classification and functional mechanisms of oncogenes and tumor suppressor genes
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics define the classes of cancer mutations and demonstrate how oncogenic and tumor-suppressive alterations disrupt cell cycle regulation and protein function.

topics.label: Mechanisms and cellular consequences of genetic instability
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain the distinctions, repair pathway failures, replication and mitotic errors, and downstream stresses that cause sequence and chromosomal instability in cancer.

topics.label: Multi-step tumor progression and hereditary cancer predisposition
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explore how stepwise mutation accumulation drives tumor progression and how inherited germline mutations accelerate this process in hereditary cancer syndromes.

topics.label: Lecture conclusion and recommended reading
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer concludes the session by confirming the learning outcomes, inviting questions, suggesting supplementary reading, and previewing the next lecture.
